title: A TESS recurrence model lowers the expected past dust duty to 0.10 in young rapid rotators
abstract: We test how selected TESS dip areas can predict earlier infrared emission. We use a released three-type recurrence model and calculate past state probabilities from all sector flags. For 762 young stars the mean on probability at 2010.5 is 0.101; for 114 selected hosts it is 0.482, and for 581 non-hosts it is 0.032. Efficiency and crowding variants give young means of 0.125 and 0.067. If material is absent in the off state, a tenfold reduction in a published infrared template is relevant. In its scalar amplitude test this reduces the young-minus-old discrepancy from 6.46 to 1.61 standard errors. The host contrast remains above its reported upper limit. This does not establish a joint dust fit. It shows that a persistent-area exclusion does not also exclude intermittent material. Flag state is not a measured dust state, and the TESS and infrared samples and flux weights differ. A matched photometric refit is still needed. We include original conditional prediction code, aggregate results, checks and exact input hashes.

display.caption: Past state probabilities from three released fits, and scalar sensitivity of the published infrared amplitude. Material presence is an extra assumption; the photometry is not refitted.

citations.reason: Released recurrence parameters; this work adds historical conditional state probabilities.
Its persistent-area infrared exclusion does not test an intermittent material model. We retain the reported infrared non-detection.
